title: Modular hosted inference surface PRD — scope controls, acceptance criteria, and launch checklist
creator: Luca Moreno
description: This PRD defines the modular hosted inference surface that unifies chat/completions/embeddings/rerank under a composable API surface. Goal: shipping a single, extensible contract and launch checklist that lets product teams use individual endpoints or compose them together (eg. embed -> rerank -> chat), with clear scope controls, backward-compatibility guarantees, SLOs, and operational runbooks. This doc captures requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout gates, and post-launch monitoring and rollback playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: API contract is published and validated by SDKs for: /v1/chat, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank
Backward-compatible behavior: clients using existing parameters retain prior semantics (compatibility matrix documented)
Structured output: chat/completions support structured output hints and schema validation; failing responses surface a clear error code
Performance SLOs: p50 latency < 120ms, p95 latency < 450ms for 2k-token mixed workload on dedicated tier; hosted baseline documented
Throughput: per-tenant sustained tokens/sec validated with canary traffic; autoscaling triggers observed under synthetic load
Cost controls: default batching + KV caching configuration applied with measurable cost reduction >= 12% for standard chat workloads
Embedding quality: end-to-end embedding similarity drift vs. baseline <= 1.0% on evaluation suite
Rerank regression: mean reciprocal rank (MRR) delta <= 0.5% from baseline on customer evaluation sets
End-to-end test coverage: integration tests in CI for compose scenarios (embed->rerank->chat) and SDK smoke tests
Observability: dashboards for token cost, per-route latency, error rates, and per-model QoS are live in Console
Security: KMS-integrated key usage validated; audit logs available for all inference calls for Private/Dedicated customers
Rollout safety: canary (1%), phased ramp (1%, 5%, 25%, 100%) with automated rollback on defined error/latency thresholds
launch_checklist: Finalize API contract and publish OpenAPI / JSON Schema; mark stable fields vs experimental
Merge SDK changes and publish v2.3.0 with compatibility shims and migration notes
Docs: end-to-end guides (compose patterns), migration guide, cost/perf tuning guide published on docs.redwood.ai
Telemetry: per-route dashboards, latency heatmaps, and per-customer cost reports configured in Console
Gating: security review completed and sign-off recorded; penetration test findings remediated
CI: add integration tests for compose flows to mainline and nightly stress tests
Canary plan: schedule, test traffic generator, rollback hooks, and on-call rotation defined
Rate limits and quotas: default quotas set, burst policies documented, and quota escalation runbook ready
Support readiness: playbooks, known issues, FAQs, and escalation contacts uploaded to internal Playbook
Legal & compliance: privacy checklist reviewed for hosted storage of prompt/response artifacts
Billing: usage metering validated end-to-end and cost reporting unit-tests present
Training: Solutions engineering brown-bag scheduled for customer-facing teams and sales enablement
Monitoring alerts: set SLO burn rate alerts and regression alerting against evaluation prompt sets
notes: Scope decision: composability limited to synchronous compose patterns for launch; async pipelines deferred to a follow-up epic
Trade-off: strict schema enforcement could break some legacy clients; opted for soft-warning deprecation window of 90 days
Performance trade-offs: we prioritized latency SLOs over maximal batching for P0 tier; batch-size tuning will be part of Optimize recommendations
Migration path: provide feature flags for customers to opt into new rerank scoring schema before enforcement
